Divisional Manager,

entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: This appeal is preferred against the award passed on 10.01.2018 by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Kollam in OP(MV) No.1700 of 2015, by the petitioners therein, claiming that the amount awarded under various heads is insufficient.
2. The petitioners, the wife and children of the deceased had filed the claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, for compensation on account of his death in a motor accident.

According to them, on 04.06.2015 at about 1.40 P.M. while the deceased was traveling by an autorickshaw through a public road, a private bus driven by the second respondent in a rash and negligent manner hit the autorickshaw and he sustained grievous injuries.
After the incident, he was taken to the hospital but later succumbed to the injuries.

3. As there is no challenge against the findings of the Tribunal regarding the cause of the motor accident, the nature of injuries suffered, the liability of the respondent, etc, the discussion hereunder MACA No.289 of 2019 4 2024:KER:83297 is limited to the essential aspects only.

4. Heard both sides and perused the available records.
5.

Learned counsel for the appellants vehemently contended that the deceased was a Homeo Practitioner, which is evident from Ext.P7 Diploma Certificate for Homeopathy Medicine and Surgery issued by the Government of Kerala and Ext.10 bank passbook which shows that there were enough bank transactions evidencing his monthly income, but the Tribunal failed to appreciate both these aspects and instead, arrived at a wrong conclusion that the evidence on record is insufficient to hold that the deceased was a Homeo Practitioner at the time of his death and erroneously fixed the notional income at the rate of Rs.10,000/-.
It is also contended that the children of the deceased were also entitled to get compensation under the head 'loss of consortium', but the Tribunal failed to award any amount on that count.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel appearing for the third respondent submitted that there is no error or illegality in the award and the Tribunal correctly arrived at a conclusion that the appellants failed to prove the monthly income of the deceased and that is the reason why his notional income was correctly fixed at the rate of Rs.10,000/-.
MACA No.289 of 2019 5 2024:KER:83297 7. It is true that the appellants did not adduce any evidence to prove the contention that the deceased was a Homeo Practitioner at the time of his death.
However, Exts.P7 and P10 documents are strenuously relied on by the learned counsel for the appellants to substantiate their contention.

Even though the documents on their face do not prove the contentions put forward, I am persuaded to accept the contention of the learned counsel for the appellants to a limited extent of re-fixing the notional income at the rate of Rs.14,000/- per month, instead of Rs.10,000/-.
It is beyond any dispute that the deceased obtained a Diploma in Homeo Medicine and Surgery from the Board of Examiner in Homeopathy, Government of Kerala in the year 1992.
Ext.P10 bank passbook also shows that there were some substantial transactions during the time of his death.
8. If the notional income is fixed as Rs.14,000/-, the appellants are entitled to get compensation under the head 'loss of dependency' at the rate of 14000x12x7x2/3=7,84,000/-.
9. The Tribunal ought to have awarded compensation for 'loss of consortium' to the children who are also in the party array.

On that head, the appellants are entitled to get an additional amount of Rs.80,000/- (40000x2).
MACA No.289 of 2019 6 2024:KER:83297

In view of the above discussion, the appeal is allowed as follows:
The appellants are entitled to get additional compensation under the following heads:-
1. Loss of dependency - Rs.2,24,000/-
2. Loss of consortium - Rs. 80,000/-
--------------

Total Rs.3,04,000/-
 ==========
The impugned award is modified only to the above extent.

Sd/-
P.KRISHNA KUMAR, JUDGE dlk 8.11.2024 Remamani vs The Divisional Manager on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134544514/
